title: Goldcrest onboarding observability intake
summary: Kickoff for Goldcrest onboarding focused on observability and network intake. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share runbook, network diagram template, and initial observability dashboard screenshots; customer to share VPC CIDR, internal SLA targets, and security questionnaire answers. Decided on 3-week pilot with canary traffic to start in staging.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we can get started. Uh, welcome Goldcrest team. This is Maya Chen, I'll be your account lead. With me is Lucas, our SE, and Priya from CSM.

[00:12] Ravi P: Hey Maya, thanks. Sofia and Ellen and Tom here. Appreciate you fitting this in. We've got about 45 minutes?

[00:18] Priya (Redwood CSM): Yep thanks, we'll aim for 45-50 so we can capture action items.

[00:25] Lucas (Redwood SE): Quick agenda — network/VPC questions, observability/tracing, runbook for pilot, and security items. Sound okay?

[00:32] Sofia: Perfect. Our main thing is making sure we can see token-level latency and cost breakdowns in staging before we go to prod. Also audit logs for queries, we have regs.

[00:42] Maya: Got it. We'll show screenshots in a sec. Before that, quick context — what's your current setup for inference? Are you planning to use Dedicated or Private?

[00:55] Ravi P: We're leaning private — all traffic must stay within our AWS account and VPC, KMS for keys. We might start with a small dedicated pool to test throughput, but Private for long term.

[01:08] Lucas: Cool — Private with a customer-managed control plane, understood. For the pilot, small Dedicated capacity can be used for quick iteration. We usually recommend dedicated for initial load testing because it avoids the handshake for VPC NATs. But if your security folks require air-gapped endpoints we can run Private.

[01:30] Ellen: The security ask is: SOC2 reports, KMS integration, and audit log retention options. Also, do you offer field-level token redaction or only whole-request redaction?

[01:45] Maya: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO attestations — we'll send the kit. KMS integrations support AWS KMS and customer-provided key policies. On redaction: currently Redwood supports redaction at the request/response granularity via transform hooks; field-level needs a small policy layer on your side or we can scope a custom pre-processor in the pilot.

[02:07] Tom: Noted. For networking, we need sample CloudFormation / Terraform for the VPC peering and route table configs. Do you require specific ENI configurations?

[02:20] Lucas: We'll share a Terraform module, and a minimal VPC diagram. For ENIs, the Private agent uses standard ENI attachments, we recommend a /24 for the initial cluster; we'll include exact ports (TCP 443, outbound 53/123 depending on NTP) in the runbook.

[02:40] Sofia: Uh, can you also show the observability — like token-level breakdown and per-route latency? Last vendor we used had token counts off by 20% which messed up cost forecasts.

[02:52] Lucas: Totally — I can screen-share, but I have to be careful with PII. (Screen share note: Lucas shared Redwood Console mock dashboard)

[03:04] Lucas: Here you can see per-route latency percentiles, token breakdown by role (user/system), and a cost estimator tied to model/quantization. The traces link to the full request payload and KV cache hit rates.

[03:22] Ravi P: That trace view is useful. Does the tracing hook propagate our internal trace IDs? We need end-to-end spans.

[03:30] Lucas: Yes — we accept traceparent headers and propagate them. We can forward spans to your X-Ray or Zipkin endpoint, or export to Datadog/Lightstep. There's an agent config flag. We'll include example config snippets.

[03:45] Ellen: How long are logs stored? We need at least 12 months of audit trails for our compliance team. Is that an enterprise add-on?

[03:55] Maya: Standard retention is 90 days; 12 months is an add-on — we'll include pricing for extended retention. Also, we can provide summarized logs with search indexes to save cost.

[04:08] Sofia: On the pilot timeline — we want a 3-week pilot: week 1 connectivity, week 2 load tests and observability checks, week 3 refine and measure. Does that align with your onboarding flow?

[04:20] Priya: Yes — that matches our recommended 3-week runway. We'll provide a checklist for each week and templates for success metrics.

[04:30] Maya: Success metrics — what matters to you? Latency SLO, cost per 1k tokens, error rate?

[04:36] Ravi P: Latency p50/p95 under 350ms for interactive flows, cost per 1k tokens below $0.20 for background batch jobs, and error rate under 0.5% for production-ish tests.

[04:50] Lucas: We can get those numbers in our perf profile and show model variant recommendations and quantization steps to meet cost goals. A quick caveat — batch workloads have different SLOs; we'll propose separate profiles.

[05:05] Tom: For the staging canary, we'll send you a sample traffic generator. Do you support continuous batching?

[05:12] Lucas: Yes — the runtime has continuous batching and adaptive batch sizing. We'll include recommended batch sizes per model and per GPU config in the runbook.

[05:25] Sofia: There's also a stakeholders question — do you need legal to sign an addendum before we exchange test data?

[05:34] Maya: For pilot we usually operate under the NDA and a pilot addendum — legal can sign the pilot agreement. We'll send the standard pilot contract and security questionnaire.

[05:44] Ellen: Please include a data flow diagram so compliance can see where tokens transit. Also, masking guidance — we need to ensure PHI and PII get redacted in app layer.

[05:55] Maya: We'll attach a sample data flow and an integration guide with recommended masking libraries.

[06:02] Priya: Quick note — handoff cadence: weekly syncs and a Slack channel. Who should own the internal updates at Goldcrest?

[06:11] Ravi P: I'll be the internal owner for infra. Sofia will own product acceptance. Ellen handles security tasks. Tom will be the SRE point.

[06:20] Maya: Great. Action items and next steps we'll capture. Lucas, anything else on the observability side?

[06:27] Lucas: One more — sampling rate for traces. We default at 10% in production, but for pilot we can set 100% to validate flows, then tune. Also, we emit KV cache hit metrics which are useful to detect wasteful re-requests.

[06:42] Sofia: That helps. On dashboards, can we get an exportable CSV of token usage per route for finance?

[06:49] Lucas: Yep — we have APIs and CSV exports. We'll give you a sample report and a billing reconciliation template.

[06:58] Tom: Network question again — any NAT gateway requirements? We prefer not to open wide egress.

[07:05] Lucas: We'll provide an egress minimal list; our agent needs to reach Redwood control plane endpoints for management — we can work with your networking team on least privilege.

[07:18] Maya: Okay, let's recap and call out owners.

[07:22] Maya: Redwood will: 1) Share onboarding runbook and Terraform VPC module (Lucas) 2) Send SOC2/ISO pack and pilot contract (Maya) 3) Provide console screenshots and sample dashboards (Lucas) 4) Provide extended retention pricing (Maya/Priya).

[07:40] Maya: Goldcrest will: 1) Share VPC CIDR and contact for networking (Ravi) 2) Return security questionnaire answers (Ellen) 3) Provide sample traffic generator and acceptance criteria (Sofia/Tom).

[07:53] Ravi P: Sounds good. Can we aim to have the runbook and diagrams by Friday? That's 3 days from now.

[07:59] Maya: Yes — we'll send initial artifacts by EOD Friday.

[08:04] Priya: I'll set up the weekly sync starting next Tuesday and create a Slack channel invite.

[08:10] Sofia: Thanks. One last thing — any recommended model variants for customer support vs summarization?

[08:17] Lucas: For support (short prompts) we suggest a trimmed LLM with KV optimizations; for summarization longer context models with chunking and higher kv cache. We'll detail in the model recommendation doc.

[08:30] Ellen: Thanks everyone, that's all from security for now.

[08:35] Maya: Great, we'll follow up with the docs. Meeting adjourned.

[08:38] (end)

Notes: occasional minor transcription glitches — e.g., Antropic mentioned as 'Antropic', and 'KV' sometimes transcribed as 'K-V', etc.
